Below is a progressive 12-week conditioning programme tailored for a 58‑year‑old male, 6 months post‑MI, cleared for Phase II cardiac rehab with the constraints you provided: keep exercise heart rate generally below 70% age‑predicted max (~115 bpm), avoid Valsalva, and avoid maximal‑effort lifting. The plan assumes access to a full gym and that client is medically stable and on any prescribed cardiac meds (e.g., beta blockers) that affect heart rate—monitor perceived exertion (RPE) in addition to HR. Use a target intensity of RPE 11–13 (light‑moderate) most sessions; interval work stays within RPE 12–14 short peaks but HR must remain < ~115 bpm. Before starting each session confirm resting HR and any new symptoms (chest pain, undue dyspnea, dizziness, palpitations). Stop or reduce intensity if symptoms develop and follow emergency protocol.

Overview and progression
- Weeks 1–4: Foundation phase — low–moderate continuous aerobic work, gentle resistance to restore muscular endurance and movement quality, mobility and breathing retraining. Focus on steady-state aerobic sessions 3×/week + 2× light resistance and flexibility/core sessions.
- Weeks 5–8: Build phase — increase aerobic duration and introduce controlled intervals (low amplitude), increase resistance volume modestly (still submax), add functional and balance work.
- Weeks 9–12: Conditioning phase — longer aerobic sessions, more structured interval work (still conservative), increased functional resistance complexity and tempo control for safety. By week 12 expect improved endurance, better work capacity within HR limits, and normal activities of daily living easier.

Monitoring and safety
- HR limit target: aim to keep exercise HR below ~115 bpm (70% APHM). Because meds may blunt HR response, use RPE 11–13 as main guide and Borg 6–20 ~ 11–13; for short intervals RPE up to 14 permissible if HR remains <115 and clinician approves.
- Avoid breath holding/Valsalva: cue slow exhale on effort, steady breathing.
- Strength loads: choose weights allowing 12–20 reps per set with no more than RPE 13 at end of set for most work. No 1RM testing.
- Warm-up: 8–12 minutes light aerobic + dynamic mobility and breathing practice each session.
- Cool-down: 6–10 minutes light cardio + static stretching, slow breathing.
- Emergency plan: trainer must have AED available and be prepared to call emergency services if chest pain, syncope, severe dyspnea occurs.

Session frequency (per week)
- Weeks 1–4: 5 sessions — 3 aerobic (30–40 min), 2 resistance/mobility (30–40 min)
- Weeks 5–8: 5–6 sessions — 3–4 aerobic (35–45 min incl. gentle intervals), 2 resistance (40 min)
- Weeks 9–12: 5–6 sessions — 3 aerobic (40–55 min incl. intervals), 2–3 resistance/functional (40–50 min)

Detailed week‑by‑week plan

Weeks 1–4: Foundation (Goals: re‑establish aerobic base, teach breathing and pacing, restore basic strength and mobility)
General session structure for each workout: Warm-up (8–12 min) → Main set → Cool-down (6–10 min) → Breathing/relaxation (2–5 min).

Week 1
- Session A — Aerobic (3×/wk: Mon/Wed/Fri)
  - Warm-up: 10 min treadmill walk at easy pace (RPE 10–11). Diaphragmatic breathing cues.
  - Main: 20–25 min continuous treadmill or recumbent bike maintaining RPE 11–12 and HR <115. If HR drifts toward 115, reduce incline/speed or switch to bike/rowing at lower effort.
  - Cool-down: 6–8 min light walking + calf/quad/hamstring stretch.
- Session B — Resistance & mobility (Tue/Thu)
  - Warm-up: 8 min bike easy.
  - Circuit x2 rounds, 40–60s rest between exercises, 90s between rounds. Use light weights (12–20 reps or until RPE ~12)
    - Seated row (cable or machine): 2×12–15
    - Chest press machine (or light dumbbell): 2×12–15
    - Leg press or sit-to-stand: 2×12–15
    - Seated dumbbell shoulder press (light, no breath-holding): 2×12–15
    - Standing calf raise (bodyweight or light): 2×15–20
    - Core: supine heel slides or pelvic tilts: 2×12–15
  - Balance/mobility: 5 min standing single‑leg hold (assisted) and gentle thoracic rotation.
  - Breathing: 3–5 min diaphragmatic breathing practice.
- Weekend: encourage two 20–30 min gentle walks (optional active recovery).

Week 2
- Aerobic sessions increase main work to 25–30 min. Add 1–2 short standing strides (30–45s) at slightly higher cadence but keep HR in limit.
- Resistance sessions: keep similar exercises, increase to 3 rounds if tolerated or add 1–2 reps per set.

Week 3

Week 4

Weeks 9–12: Conditioning (Goals: extend endurance, introduce more structured interval conditioning, maintain/respect cardiac limits while improving functional capacity)

    - Incline chest press 3×10–12

- Resistance: maintain 3 sets, progress a little on load only if all sets end at RPE ≤13.

Week 11

- Resistance: introduce more functional/compound sequence but maintain low‑moderate loads and higher reps (10–15). Add a mobility/functional session focusing on hip/shoulder ROM and balance.

Week 12 (tapered consolidation)

- Resistance: 2 sessions this week, lighter volume (2 sets per exercise) to avoid excessive fatigue.
- Finish with reassessment of perceived exertion, ability to tolerate daily activities, and set maintenance plan (2–3 aerobic sessions/week + 2 resistance sessions/week ongoing).

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Hydration: maintain adequate hydration; sip fluids before/during/after sessions if tolerated. Avoid heavy sodium/fat meals immediately before exercise; follow physician guidance.
- Pre‑exercise snack: light carbohydrate (e.g., banana, toast) 30–60 min before session if needed to avoid lightheadedness.

- Medications: confirm timing relative to exercise; e.g., beta blockers blunt HR—emphasise RPE rather than HR alone.
- Sleep and stress: encourage 7–8 hrs sleep, and daily breathing practice (5–10 min diaphragmatic breathing) to support vagal tone and recovery.
- Recovery days: include active recovery like gentle walking, mobility work, or yoga. Avoid high intensity on consecutive days; ensure at least one full rest day/week.

Progression and modifications
- If HR regularly exceeds prescribed limit: reduce intensity/duration, switch to lower‑impact modality (bike/recumbent stepper/elliptical), lengthen recovery intervals.
- If symptomatic (angina, undue shortness of breath, lightheadedness): stop and follow medical protocol.
- Strength progression: increase load only when sets are attained with RPE ≤12 for two consecutive sessions. Prefer adding reps first, then small load increments (~5–10%).

Below is the full, integrated 12‑week conditioning programme for your 58‑year‑old male client post‑MI. It includes the original Phase II foundation, planned Phase III progression, the interval additions, and the conservative regression back to Phase II after the chest‑tightness event — all merged into one usable timeline. The plan highlights week‑by‑week sessions, aerobic/strength details, interval progressions, monitoring rules, nutrition/recovery guidance, and clear conditions for stepping up or pulling back intensity.

Summary of medical/training rules to follow throughout
- Baseline precautions (unless cardiologist gives different written instructions): 
  - Age-predicted max ≈ 162 bpm (220 − 58). 
  - Phase II HR cap: ~70% APHM ≈ 115 bpm. Phase III HR cap: ~85% APHM ≈ 138–140 bpm (use exact cap from cardiologist). Use the current active cap per cardiology guidance.
  - RPE guidance: Phase II use RPE 11–13 primarily; Phase III allow RPE 12–15 for short peaks. If on beta blockers, prioritize RPE.
  - Valsalva: Phase II — avoid. Phase III — moderate Valsalva allowed at moderate loads only, under supervision; no maximal Valsalva or heavy singles.
  - Strength: avoid maximal loading or 1RM testing at all times; progress via reps/sets and small load increases.
- Symptom rules: stop immediately for chest pain, significant breathlessness, dizziness, syncope, or palpitations. Follow emergency procedures.
- Monitoring: use chest‑strap HR monitor; log resting HR, peak HR, 1‑min recovery HR, RPE, BP (periodically), meds and timing, and any symptoms.

Overview — phases and progression
- Weeks 1–4 (Phase II Foundation): rebuild aerobic base, breathing technique, movement quality; light resistance training (high reps, submax).
- Weeks 5–7 (Phase II Build): increase aerobic duration, introduce cautious short bursts and modest resistance progressions (still Phase II limits).
- Week 8: Planned transition toward Phase III — start conservative progressions and interval introduction. (Note: this is where the Phase III block originally began.)
- Week 9: Client experienced chest tightness during intervals. Immediately de-escalate and revert to Phase II constraints.
- Weeks 9–12: Conservative Phase II retraining while awaiting cardiology re‑evaluation. (If/when cardiology clears Phase III again, follow the Phase III progression in Weeks 8–12 as previously detailed; see criteria for re‑escalation.)

Detailed week‑by‑week programme

Weeks 1–4 — Phase II Foundation (Goals: safe aerobic base, breathing, mobility, low‑intensity strength)
General session layout: Warm-up 8–12 min (light aerobic + mobility + diaphragmatic breathing) → Main set → Cool-down 6–10 min (light aerobic + static stretch + breathing).

Week 1
- Mon — Aerobic: Treadmill or recumbent bike 20–25 min steady at RPE 11–12. HR ≤ ~115. Warm‑up/cool‑down included.
- Tue — Strength (light): Machines/assisted/free 1 circuit ×1–2 rounds: Seated row 12–15; Chest press 12–15; Sit‑to‑stand 12–15; Seated DB shoulder press 12–15; Calf raises 15–20; Dead bug 12 each. Balance 2×20s. Controlled tempo. No Valsalva.
- Wed — Active recovery: 20–30 min gentle walk + mobility.
- Thu — Aerobic: Bike 25–30 min steady RPE 11–12.
- Fri — Strength (light): Repeat Tue circuit, 1–2 rounds; add glute bridge 2×12–15.
- Sat — Optional light walk 20–30 min.
- Sun — Rest.

Week 2
- Aerobic sessions increase to 25–30 min. Add 1–2 short easy build efforts (30–45s) only if HR remains well below cap.
- Strength: Progress to 2 circuits or 2 sets per exercise if tolerated; maintain 12–18 reps and RPE ≤13.

Week 3
- Aerobic: 30 min continuous or 3×8–10 min bouts with 2–3 min easy recovery between.
- Strength: Add one unilateral movement (assisted single‑leg Romanian deadlift to chair, 2×10 each). Maintain technique emphasis.

Week 4
- Aerobic: 30–35 min continuous at RPE 11–13. Introduce one session with brief gentle intervals: 4×2 min slightly higher cadence at RPE 12–13 with 2–3 min easy recovery (keep HR ≤115).
- Strength: 2–3 rounds circuit, 12–15 reps, controlled tempo. Add scapular stability Y/T raises 2×12.

Weeks 5–7 — Phase II Build (Goals: increase duration, strength endurance; remain conservative)
Week 5
- Aerobic: Two steady 35–40 min RPE 11–13 sessions + one controlled interval session: 6×2 min at RPE 12–13 with 2–3 min recovery (monitor HR).
- Strength: 2 sessions/week, 2–3 sets ×12–15 reps for machines and supported free weight variations. Add farmer carry light 3×30–45s.
- Mobility/breathing: 5–10 min daily.

Week 6
- Aerobic: Steady sessions 40 min. Interval session: 6×3 min at RPE 12–13 with 2–3 min recovery; prefer bike/elliptical if treadmill spiked HR.
- Strength: Progress load modestly only if RPE ≤12; include Romanian deadlift 3×10, step‑ups 3×10 each.

Week 7
- Aerobic: Steady 40 min; interval session: 5×4 min at RPE 12–13 with 2–3 min recovery. Rotate modalities to control HR response.
- Strength: Superset structure for time efficiency; stay with 12–15 reps and submax loads.

Week 8 — Planned Phase III transition (conservative start)
- Intended plan (only if cardiology clearance): begin higher intensity work and Phase III strength progressions. However, this week we begin conservative steps that will be paused if symptoms occur.
- Aerobic:
  - Two steady sessions: 40–45 min at RPE 11–13.
  - One planned interval session: 4×4 min at RPE 13–14 with 3 min recovery. (Monitor HR closely and stop intervals if chest discomfort occurs.)
- Strength:
  - Two sessions with modest progression: 3 sets exercise, some compound lifts in 8–12 rep range if tolerated (still conservative).
  - Valsalva: still avoid unless explicitly allowed by cardiology for specific lifts.

Week 9 — Incident and immediate regression to Phase II
- Event: client experienced chest tightness during last week’s interval work.
- Immediate actions taken (and maintained now):
  - All interval work stopped; revert to Phase II rules immediately: HR cap back to ≈115 bpm; RPE target 11–13; no Valsalva; strength limited to high‑rep submax (12–20).
  - Suspend any plans for Phase III intervals or moderate Valsalva until cardiology re‑evaluates and clears.
- Week 9 plan (Phase II retrain)
  - Mon — Aerobic: Recumbent bike 20–25 min steady RPE 11–12.
  - Tue — Strength (light): Machines/cables, 1–2 sets ×12–15 (Seated row, Chest press, Leg press/sit‑to‑stand, Seated press, Glute bridges, Core).
  - Wed — Active recovery: 20–30 min walk + breathing practice.

Weeks 10–12 — Continued Phase II conservative retraining until re‑evaluation (or re‑escalation if cardiology clears)
General approach: keep aerobic steady work moderate, maintain light strength, emphasis on symptom‑free progression and conservative increases only after multiple symptom‑free sessions.

Week 10
- Aerobic:
  - 3 sessions/week: 25–35 min steady at RPE 11–13 on recumbent bike, treadmill walking, or pool.
  - No intervals or bursts above RPE 13.
- Strength:
  - 2 sessions/week, 2 sets ×12–18 reps. Exercises: Seated row, Chest press, Leg press or sit‑to‑stand, Romanian deadlift light, Seated shoulder press, Glute bridge, Pallof press, core.
- Mobility/breathing: daily 5–10 min diaphragmatic breathing and thoracic mobility.
- Continue logging HR, RPE and any symptoms.

Week 11
- Aerobic:
  - Aim for 30–35 min steady sessions (3×/week) at RPE 11–13; progress by 5 min only if symptom‑free across multiple sessions.
- Strength:
  - 2 sessions/week with 2–3 sets of 12–18 reps if tolerated. Continue functional and balance work.
- Active recovery: light walks and pool sessions on off days.

Week 12
- Aerobic:
  - Consolidate: 3×/week, 30–40 min steady at RPE 11–13. Keep total weekly moderate aerobic volume conservative (~90–150 min) depending on tolerance.
- Strength:
  - 2 sessions with reduced volume if any concern: 2 sets ×12–15 reps. Maintain technique, breathing cues and pain/symptom vigilance.
- Reassessment:
  - At end of week 12 (or earlier if cardiology re‑evaluates), compile logs (HR, RPE, symptoms) and share with cardiology for decision on resuming Phase III progressions. If cardiology clears, follow the Phase III progression previously outlined (see Phase III block below).

Phase III block (what to do if/when cardiology re‑clears)
- Summary of Phase III progression (previously planned for weeks 8–12): raise HR cap to ~85% APHM (≈138–140 bpm), allow moderate Valsalva on moderate loads, introduce interval conditioning and moderate‑load strength (sets in 6–12 rep range) with supervision. Progress intervals from conservative (4×4 min) to varied (1–2 min short pushes, 4–6 min efforts) and add one interval session/week initially, moving to two only after stable responses.
- Re‑escalation criteria to begin Phase III:
  - Written cardiology clearance with exact HR cap and Valsalva guidance.
  - Symptom‑free Phase II sessions for the period cardiologist specifies (commonly 7–14 days or per clinician).
  - Stable physiologic responses in supervised sessions (HR, BP, recovery).
- If cleared, reintroduce intervals gradually (e.g., 4×2–4 min @ RPE 13–14 with full monitoring) and progress per earlier interval plan only under supervision.

Interval conditioning (only after cardiology clearance)
- If cleared to resume, interval plan begins conservatively:
  - Start: 4×4 min @ RPE 13–14 with 3 min recovery (week 1 of Phase III re‑start).
  - Progress: increase work duration, reduce recovery, or increase repetition count gradually; short higher‑intensity 1 min pushes (RPE 14–15) only if HR remains ≤ cap and under supervision.
- If any recurrence of chest tightness during intervals, immediately stop and revert to Phase II restrictions and notify cardiology.

Nutrition and recovery (applies across all phases)
- Cardiac‑focused Mediterranean style: vegetables, fruit, whole grains, legumes, nuts, seeds, fatty fish 2–3×/week, olive oil as main fat. Limit red/processed meats, refined sugars, excessive saturated fat; aim for 25–35 g fiber/day and sodium <2,000 mg/day (or per physician).
- Protein: 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day during Phase II to preserve lean mass. Increase to 1.0–1.4 g/kg/day if Phase III strength increases (confirm renal status).
- Pre/post workout: light carb 30–60 min before if needed (banana, toast); carb+protein within 1–2 hours after sessions.
- Hydration: maintain; be mindful if on diuretics—consult cardiologist.
- Sleep & stress: prioritize 7–8 hours sleep; daily breathing practice 5–10 min to aid vagal tone.
- Supplements: only with physician approval (omega‑3s, vit D if deficient); avoid unapproved or high‑dose supplements.

Monitoring, documentation and communication
- Record for every session: date/time, modality, warm‑up time, main set (duration/intensity), peak HR, 1‑min recovery HR, RPE, BP if taken pre/post, medications and timing, and any symptoms (type, duration, response).
- After chest tightness event: send a summary to cardiology immediately. Include HR logs, session notes and any interventions taken.
- Trainer should request explicit cardiology guidance in writing for HR cap, Valsalva use, allowed intensities, and tests required prior to resuming Phase III.

Emergency and symptom protocol
- For chest pain that persists despite rest and prescribed nitroglycerin (if applicable) → call emergency services immediately.
- For syncope, severe dyspnea, or signs of unstable arrhythmia → stop exercise, call emergency services.
- For recurrent chest tightness during supervised low‑intensity exercise → stop training, monitor vitals, contact cardiology for urgent review.

Progression rules and decision flow (quick)
- Phase II progression (upgrades within Phase II): increase session duration by 5–10 min or add ~1 interval (low amplitude) only if 2–3 consecutive symptom‑free sessions at current workload and HR responses stable.
- Escalation to Phase III: requires written cardiology clearance.
- If symptoms occur at any point, revert immediately to Phase II conservative plan and notify cardiology.
- If cardiology clears to Phase III again, resume Phase III plan starting at conservative Phase III entry (lower end of HR cap/duration) and progress incrementally.

Sample 12‑week at‑a‑glance (condensed)
- Weeks 1–4: Phase II foundation — 3 aerobic steady + 2 strength/week; 20–35 min aerobic; strength 12–20 reps, 1–3 sets.
- Weeks 5–7: Phase II build — 35–40 min steady, one cautious short‑interval session by week 5–7 (low amplitude), strength 2–3 sets ×12–15.
- Week 8: Begin conservative Phase III transition (planned intervals and moderate strength) — only proceed if cardiology cleared.
- Week 9: Chest tightness event → immediate regression back to Phase II. All interval/Phase III elements stopped.
- Weeks 9–12: Conservative Phase II retraining while awaiting cardiology re‑evaluation — 3 steady aerobic/week (20–35 min), 2 light strength/week (12–20 reps), no Valsalva, no intervals.
- Post‑12 weeks: follow cardiologist clearance to either continue Phase II progression or reintroduce Phase III elements (intervals, moderate load strength with moderate Valsalva if allowed).
